_meta.indication: VIMIZIM (elosulfase alfa) is indicated for patients with Mucopolysaccharidosis type IVA (MPS IVA; Morquio A syndrome)

pivotal_trials.design: 24-week, multinational (17 countries), multicenter (31 clinical sites), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study evaluating elosulfase alfa 2.0 mg/kg once weekly and 2.0 mg/kg every other week versus placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with MPS IVA (Morquio A syndrome), ages 5 to 57 years
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change from baseline in the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) distance at Week 24
pivotal_trials.n: 176 patients randomized/ITT (placebo 59, 2.0 mg/kg once weekly 58, 2.0 mg/kg every other week 59)
pivotal_trials.result: For elosulfase alfa 2.0 mg/kg once weekly vs placebo, LS mean difference in Week 24 change from baseline 6MWT was 22.5 meters (95% CI 4.0, 40.9; p=0.0174); the every-other-week dose was not superior (LS mean difference 0.5 meters; 95% CI -17.8, 18.9; p=0.9542)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) are pyrexia (33% vs 14% placebo), vomiting (31% vs 7%), headache (26% vs 15%), nausea (24% vs 7%), abdominal pain (21% vs 2%), chills (10% vs 2%), and fatigue (10% vs 3%). Hypersensitivity reactions occurred in 44 of 235 (18.7%) patients, and 18 of 235 (7.7%) experienced signs/symptoms consistent with anaphylaxis
target_moa: Elosulfase alfa is a recombinant human N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase, the lysosomal enzyme deficient in MPS IVA; it provides exogenous enzyme that hydrolyzes sulfate from keratan sulfate and chondroitin-6-sulfate, reducing their lysosomal accumulation

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS INCLUDING ANAPHYLAXIS and RISK OF ACUTE RESPIRATORY COMPLICATIONS — life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have occurred; initiate VIMIZIM in a healthcare setting with appropriate monitoring and support; patients with acute respiratory illness may be at risk of serious acute exacerbation of respiratory compromise

advisory_committee.vote: The Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) met November 19, 2013; the majority of the Committee considered the 6MWT adequate for evaluating treatment benefit in MPS IVA patients

orphan_indication.text: Elosulfase alfa (recombinant human N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase) was granted Orphan Product designation in May 2009 for the treatment of MPS IVA (Morquio A syndrome)

summary.text: Vimizim (elosulfase alfa), an enzyme replacement therapy for the rare lysosomal storage disease MPS IVA (Morquio A syndrome), received orphan product designation in May 2009 and was approved first-cycle under priority review on the basis of a single pivotal placebo-controlled trial (MOR-004) with the 6MWT primary endpoint, following review by the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC)

citations.quote: In May 2009, Orphan Product designation was granted.
BLA 125460 was submitted on March 29, 2013 and granted priority review; however, a solicited major amendment submitted May 10, 2013 resulted in an extension of the user fee goal date.
The efficacy of the BMN 110 2.0 mg/kg/week dose was primarily supported by a single trial MOR-004.

On November 19, 2013, the Division sought advice from the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) regarding the appropriateness of the 6MWT to assess treatment benefit in this patient population.
